notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); no hardware was attached or run. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the python-object family and PythonObjectDriver, but this is a direct Driver. The upstream Tecan class builds an XML GenericCommand for every operation and sends it through the .NET Tecan.VisionX.API.V2 Execution Channel (tecan_fluent/tecan_ctrl.py:12-17,41-44), and its pipetting methods take volume lists, tip lists and well lists; a command table is not the right shape for a vendor SDK robot, and the guide's shape for one is a direct Driver with decorated methods, per-field limits and a safe-state action. A serial or SCPI shape would also have to invent a wire syntax the clone does not contain. The six actions are x-cap extension ids because the catalogue's cap.fluid.aspirate.v1 and cap.fluid.dispense.v1 have no liquid-class or LiHa-tip input; the exact upstream interface needs both, as the catalogue_requests explain. NOT COVERED: add_labware, liha_get_tips, liha_drop_tips, liha_set_tips_back, mca_get_head_adapter, mca_get_tips, mca_drop_tips, mca_drop_tips_back_to_source and run_command (it takes a .NET ICommand object), and the RuntimeController functions other than StopMethod and GetFluentStatus. The MCA partial-tip and offset features are not exposed because the clone says they are not implemented (README.md:147-151). The volume, tip-index and mix-cycle inputs are Limit.operator_required: no text file of the clone states those ranges, so every call is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site supplies site-limits.json; site-limits.example.json is an illustrative overlay, not a device bound. No independent hardware e-stop is documented in the clone, so estop_physical_ref is not set; the safe-state action x-cap.angli339.stop.v1 satisfies SAFE-045, and the @estop calls RuntimeController.StopMethod() and then detaches the channel so run_command refuses further commands (tecan_fluent/tecan_ctrl.py:41-44). An accepted operator reset re-attaches the channel the e-stop detached; the upstream object has no reset call. The hardware backend (native.py) was never run: it imports tecan_fluent only on the hardware path, needs pythonnet and a Windows FluentControl installation, and the loader refuses this model-authored R2 package until a human sets reviewed_by. The fake is an in-memory object, not a recording; its status words, channel object and recorded calls are placeholders. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-30; reviewed_by stays null): accepted; the reviewer changed no file of the package. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
